# 5 Senses — Together to the Core

A two-player game of friendly rivalry and shared responsibility. Two humans share a screen. One blue explorer (Blu), one coral explorer (Ember), and a 20-sided die. Estimated play time: 15–25 minutes. This first edition has no solo mode, AI opponent, or online multiplayer.

## Goal

Restore all five sense beacons and bring BOTH explorers to the core (space 24). Only then compare scores: highest wins; ties share the crown. If shared power falls to zero, both lose regardless of score.

## Setup

Both explorers start on space 0, with 0 points. All five beacons are off. Shared power starts at 3, its maximum. Blue takes the first turn. Change player names in Settings when starting a new game.

## A turn

1. **Roll a d20, or recharge.** Rolls 1–5 move 1 space; 6–10 move 2; 11–15 move 3; 16–20 move 4. A natural 20 also gives the rolling player 5 points. Recharging replaces the entire turn: stay put and add 1 shared power, up to 3. Recharge is available only below 3 power.
2. **Follow the single spiral route.** Move forward. An unrestored beacon at space 4, 8, 12, 16, or 20 stops the move early; unused movement is discarded. Resolve a joint repair instead of a normal challenge. Landing on a restored beacon gives a normal snapshot challenge for that beacon's sense.
3. **Otherwise, take a snapshot challenge.** Choose Safe (3 memory cards) or Bold (5 cards). Look as long as you need, hide the cards, then identify which word occupied the requested position. Safe gives +5 for correct, 0 for wrong. Bold gives +15 for correct, −5 for wrong. A score never falls below zero. The other player does not help with solo snapshots.
4. **Pass the turn** after resolving the challenge or repair, arriving at the core, or recharging. A repair failure must be retried before any turn can continue.

## Repairing a beacon

The entire game pauses at an unrestored beacon. Both players may talk and help each other memorize a four-digit code, using the numbers 1–4. There is no timer. Hide the code when ready.

- Blue enters the first two digits; Coral enters the final two, regardless of whose move triggered the repair.
- The full code is checked after both halves are submitted.
- Correct: the beacon stays on permanently, both players gain 10 points, and the triggering player's turn ends.
- Wrong: lose 1 shared power. At 0 power the team loses. Otherwise retry the same beacon with a newly generated code. There is no recharge or normal movement during a repair.
- Each player can undo their first digit before entering their second. Entering the second digit locks that player's half.

Tip: Recharge before rolling when power is low. Make a plan together before hiding a repair code.

## The core and the winner

You do not need an exact roll: movement is capped at space 24. Each player earns a one-time 10-point arrival bonus, and takes no snapshot challenge on arrival. A finished explorer waits at the core while the other takes consecutive turns. Once both are home and all five beacons are on, highest score wins the rivalry. Equal scores share the crown. Both players succeeded as a team.

## Example

Blu is on space 2 and rolls 14: normally 3 steps. The first unrestored beacon is on space 4, so Blu stops there and discards the remaining step. Blu and Ember repair Sight together. They each gain 10 points, and Ember takes the next turn. Later, Ember rolls a natural 20: Ember gains 5 bonus points and moves up to 4 spaces, still stopping at any unrestored beacon.

## Accessible play

All snapshot challenges use readable, sense-themed words. Smell and taste are imagined; there are no real substances or objects to identify. Sound effects are optional and off by default. There are no timers and no required sensory deprivation activities. Numbers and labels accompany color. Gentle mode reduces motion and glow. The route below the board provides text positions. Either player can take as much time as needed.

## Saving and controls

Progress saves automatically in this browser when browser storage is available. Refreshing during a snapshot returns to its difficulty choice; refreshing during a repair starts its code over without restoring spent power. This is a casual shared-screen game, not a secure competitive system. Drag the board to orbit, scroll to zoom, or use the view controls. Settings can start a new game after explicit reset confirmation. The downloadable GLB contains the modeled tabletop and three clay-style characters; it is a digital scene, not a certified print-ready manufacturing model.

## Design notes

The five sense beacons preserve the original game's collective-restoration idea. A d20 replaces the ordinary die, with four movement bands that keep the board pace manageable. Optional risk changes scoring without skipping cooperation. A shared power reserve makes recharging a strategic contribution. The handmade blue and coral figures become explorers; the gray figure watches over the core.
